fine_lines.title: used to vs would
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان يصفان شيئًا تكرر في الماضي. الفرق 1: نستخدم would فقط إذا ذكرنا الفترة الزمنية أولًا (When I first started here, I would go every day). الفرق 2: مع أفعال الحالة مثل be, think, feel, see, understand نستخدم used to فقط (It used to be across from the cafeteria).
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both describe repeated past actions. Difference 1: use would only when you say the time period first (When I first started here, I would go every day). Difference 2: with state verbs like be, think, feel, see, understand, use only used to (It used to be across from the cafeteria).

examples.sentence: When I was a child, I would play outside every day.
I used to be a very important person.
I used to sing with my family.

fine_lines.title: lose vs lost
fine_lines.explanation_ar: lose فعل في المضارع (يُضيِّع)، و lost هو الماضي والتصريف الثالث. وتأتي lost صفة بمعنى ضائع أو تائه: I'm lost.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Lose is the present verb; lost is the past and past participle. Lost is also an adjective: I'm lost (I don't know where I am).

examples.sentence: I lost my key this morning.
I'm lost. Where is the station?

grammar.title: Used to and would for past habits
grammar.explanation_ar: used to + فعل (المصدر): لعادة أو حالة في الماضي انتهت الآن (I used to sing all the time). النفي: didn't use to، والسؤال: Did you use to...? / What did you use to do? (بدون d). would + فعل: لعادة متكررة في الماضي، ونستخدمها بعد ذكر الزمن (When I first started working here, I would go every day). لا نستخدم would مع أفعال الحالة (be, think, feel, see, understand)، بل used to: It used to be across from the cafeteria.
grammar.explanation_en: Used to + verb: a past habit or state that is not true now (I used to sing all the time). Negative: didn't use to; question: Did you use to...? (no d). Would + verb: a repeated past action, after you say the time (When I first started working here, I would go every day). Don't use would with state verbs (be, think, feel, see, understand); use used to: It used to be across from the cafeteria.
examples: It used to be across from the cafeteria.
When I first started working here, I would go every day!
As a child, what did you use to do to feel happy?
When I was little, I used to sing all the time.

questions.question: The office ____ across from the cafeteria. Now it's in the basement.
questions.explanation_ar: be فعل حالة فنستخدم used to be.
questions.explanation_en: Be is a state verb, so use used to be.

questions.question: When I was young, I ____ play outside every day.
questions.explanation_ar: ذكرنا الزمن أولًا، ففعل متكرر مع would صحيح.
questions.explanation_en: The time is given first, so would is correct for a repeated action.

questions.question: What did you ____ do as a child?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد did نستخدم use to بدون d.
questions.explanation_en: After did, use 'use to' without d.

questions.question: Which sentence is WRONG?
choices: I used to live in Cairo.
As a child, I would be very shy.
As a child, I used to be very shy.
When I was ten, I would ride my bike.
questions.explanation_ar: be فعل حالة، فلا نستخدم معه would، بل used to be.
questions.explanation_en: Be is a state verb, so use used to be, not would be.

questions.question: The bank is ____ the park. (on the other side)
questions.explanation_en: Across from means on the other side of.

questions.question: 'Used to' talks about:
choices: past habits that are not true now
questions.explanation_ar: used to لعادات في الماضي انتهت.
questions.explanation_en: Used to is for past habits that stopped.
